newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's STET in alliance with AT&T.
newsitem.headline: Italy's STET in alliance with AT&T.

text.p: Italy's STET/Telecom Italia and AT&T Corp of the United States on Wednesday ended a rash of media speculation by announcing they were forging a strategic global telecoms alliance with a focus on Latin America and Europe.
"We've really scored. With this accord Stet/Telecom has built the foundation for our projection into the world," the president of soon-to-be-privatised Stet, Guido Rossi, said at a news conference.
The agreement will be finalised by the end of the year, he added. No financial details were disclosed.
In Europe, STET/Telecom Italia will join the AT&T-Unisource telecoms joint venture, with the option of taking up to 30 percent of AT&T-Unisource.
Unisource, the grouping of Dutch PTT, Telia of Sweden and Swiss Telecom PTT, currently owns 60 percent of pan-European business telecoms venture AT&T-Unisource. AT&T holds the remaining 40 percent.

STET/Telecom Italia plans to distribute AT&T-Unisource services in Italy. In return the Italian group will transfer into AT&T-Unisource the relevant business activities of data and telecoms unit Telemedia International (TMI).
In Latin America, STET/Telecom Italia and AT&T will form a 50-50 joint venture to deliver a portfolio of global services.

Stet managing director Tomaso Tommasi di Vignano told reporters that the deal for Latin America "will lead to enormous opportunities even in the next few months", including a joint bid with AT&T for a cellular phone licence in Brazil.
"Within the next four years, we expect the telecoms market in Latin America to grow 70 percent," he said, adding that Stet already has $2.0 billion in assets in the region.
Both AT&T and Stet officials agreed it was too early to say whether the U.S. company would take a stake in Stet.
"A decision on a possible share swap will be taken by the middle of September," Rossi added after the conference. Stet is set to be privatised in October.
Stet's statutes envisage a maximum three percent stake for private shareholders with the possibility of five percent with Treasury approval.

Earlier, AT&T Corp president John Walter told Reuters that it was "premature at this particular point to speculate. The Italian government has yet to define specifics associated with the privatisation".
Asked if AT&T wanted a stake in STET, Walter said the most important thing was that AT&T had a very strong alliance that satisfied its customers' expectations.
"That does not require an equity investment but at the same time equity investments...do create a stronger business model and it's something we're open to," Walter said.

STET/Telecom Italia announced the news in a statement issued jointly with AT&T and Netherlands-based Unisource, ending long-running media speculation about whether the U.S. and Italian groups would get together.

The speculation had flared after Telefonica of Spain was asked to leave Unisource NV in April after forming an alliance with AT&T rival Concert, the British Telecom Plc /MCI Communications Corp partnership.
Telefonica's move had raised questions about AT&T- Unisource's ability to compete globally with Concert and Global One, the venture grouping Sprint Corp, France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom.
"It's something that was expected, it was a logical step. AT&T's found a replacement for Telefonica," said one telecoms analyst, declining to be named.
"Telefonica has been flavour of the month because it has a very strong presence in Latin America, STET has some clout there but nowhere near that of Telefonica," said another.
The Italian group's Latin American venture with AT&T will deliver a portfolio of global services via two newly formed pan-American operating entities, the statement said.

One will serve multinational customers, large and medium-sized businesses, and high-end consumers throughout the region. The other will offer telecoms transport services to the region's telecommunications providers.

"The alliance between STET/Telecom Italia and AT&T is based on the complementary expertise and strong local presence of the two partners and their affiliates in Latin America," the statement, issued in the Netherlands, said.
